newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices steady - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices steady - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were steady as strength from earlier in the week faded on increased hog marketings and lighter packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold fully steady at $56.50 to $57.50 per cwt in the country and $57.50 to $58.50, with a few at $59.00 for hogs at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $57.50 to $58.50 in the country and up to $59.00 at plants, sources there said.
Indiana hogs sold steady at $56.50-$57.00 in the country and $58.00-$58.50, few at $59.00 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $55.50 to $56.50 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants, sources there said.
Packer demand also was lighter amid further slaughter reductions as companies continue to fight unprofitable operating margins, they said.
Larger-than-expected interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts on Wednesday also drained some of the strength in hog prices apparent earlier this week, sources said.
The interior run Wednesday in the Iowa/southern Minnesota area totaled 102,000 head, slightly above the estimate of 100,000, USDA reported.
